faqs.q: The Cross Roads case, which held that freedom of circulation is essential to freedom of the press, arose from a banning order issued under which state's Maintenance of Public Order Act?
faqs.e: The case is Romesh Thappar vs. State of Madras (1950), concerning Article 19(1)(a). As a sequel, the 1st Amendment Act (1951) added "public order" as a reasonable restriction under Article 19(2), a ground the Court had refused to accept in this judgement.

faqs.q: In A.K. Gopalan vs. State of Madras (1950), the Supreme Court held that the expression "procedure established by law" under Article 21 does not carry the same meaning as which American constitutional expression?
faqs.e: This narrow, textualist interpretation confined Article 21's protection to arbitrary executive action alone, and held the field from 1950 until it was overruled in Maneka Gandhi (1978).

faqs.q: Which Section of the Preventive Detention Act, 1950 was invalidated in the A.K. Gopalan case for violating Article 22?
The Communal GO struck down in State of Madras vs. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) was held to violate which Articles of the Constitution?
The Champakam Dorairajan judgement led to the insertion of which new clause in Article 15, permitting special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes?
faqs.e: Inserted by the 1st Amendment Act (1951), this clause effectively nullified the judgement's effect.

faqs.q: In Shankari Prasad vs. Union of India (1951), the Supreme Court held that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 also extends to which Part of the Constitution?
faqs.e: The Court ruled that the word "law" in Article 13(2) refers only to ordinary law and not constituent law made under Article 368, upholding the 1st Amendment Act (1951). This stance was reaffirmed in Sajjan Singh (1964) but overruled in Golak Nath (1967).

faqs.q: The Berubari Union case (1960) held that cession of Indian territory to a foreign state requires an amendment under Article 368 altering which Schedule?
Which Amendment Act gave effect to the transfer of the Berubari Union territory to Pakistan, following the Supreme Court's 1960 ruling?
faqs.e: The transfer was carried out under the 1958 Indo-Pak Agreement (Nehru-Noon Agreement).

faqs.q: The K.M. Nanavati case (1961), concerning the murder of his wife's paramour, brought out shortcomings that ultimately led to the abolition of which system of trial in India?
faqs.e: The system was fully removed only by the new Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, though this case exposed its flaws.

faqs.q: In I.C. Golak Nath vs. State of Punjab (1967), the Supreme Court held that a constitutional amendment act is a "law" within the meaning of which Article?
The Golak Nath judgement applied which doctrine to give its ruling only prospective, and not retrospective, operation?
Which Amendment Act was enacted as a sequel to the Golak Nath case, providing that Parliament has power to amend any part of the Constitution including fundamental rights?
The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) is credited with the emergence of which doctrine as a limitation on Parliament's amending power?
faqs.e: The Court overruled Golak Nath (1967) and upheld the 24th Amendment Act (1971), holding that Parliament can amend any provision including fundamental rights, except the basic structure.

faqs.q: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court validated which Amendment Act, passed the same year as the 24th and 25th Amendments?
In Indira Nehru Gandhi vs. Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court struck down Clause (4) of which Article, which had barred election disputes involving the Prime Minister from judicial review?
Clause (4) of Article 329A, struck down in the Indira Nehru Gandhi case, had been inserted by which Amendment Act?
The A.D.M. Jabalpur case (1976), popularly known as the Habeas Corpus case, upheld the constitutional validity of Section 16A(9) of which Act?
faqs.e: The Court held that if Article 21's enforcement is suspended under Article 359, a detenu has no locus standi to move a writ under Article 226. This ruling is no longer good law.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act nullified the A.D.M. Jabalpur ruling by providing that Article 21's enforcement cannot be suspended by a Presidential Order?

Consider the following propositions laid down in Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India (1978):
(I) Articles 14, 19 and 21 are not mutually exclusive
(II) The expression "personal liberty" in Article 21 is of the widest amplitude
(III) The right to life includes only physical existence and excludes human dignity
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Court actually held the right to "live" includes the right to live with human dignity, making statement (III) false.

faqs.q: The Maneka Gandhi judgement overruled the restrictive interpretation of Article 21 laid down in which earlier case?
Which rule, establishing the inter-relation of Articles 14, 19 and 21, was firmly established by the Maneka Gandhi judgement?
faqs.e: The judgement also introduced the American concept of "due process of law" into Indian judicial interpretation, reversing the position taken in A.K. Gopalan.

faqs.q: In Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab (1980), the Supreme Court held that the death penalty for murder should be confined to which category of cases?
faqs.e: The Court upheld Section 302 IPC's death penalty provision as not violative of Articles 19 or 21, but held it must be an exception rather than the rule.

faqs.q: The Minerva Mills case (1980) invalidated Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, along with the amendment to which other Article, both inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976)?
faqs.e: The Court held that the limited amending power of Parliament, judicial review, and the harmony between fundamental rights and directive principles are all basic features of the Constitution.

faqs.q: Waman Rao vs. Union of India (1980) held that amendments to the Ninth Schedule made after which date are open to challenge on the ground that they damage the basic structure?
faqs.e: This is the date on which the Kesavananda Bharati verdict was delivered; amendments to the Ninth Schedule before this date were held valid.

faqs.q: In the Shah Bano case (1985), the Supreme Court held that which Section of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is secular in character and prevails over personal law in case of conflict?
Which Act was enacted in 1986 to overturn the effect of the Shah Bano judgement by limiting maintenance to the period of iddat?

options.c: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act

faqs.a: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act
faqs.e: In the Danial Latifi case (2001), the Supreme Court upheld this Act's validity but held a Muslim husband liable to pay maintenance even beyond the iddat period.

faqs.q: D.C. Wadhwa vs. State of Bihar (1986) held that the ordinance-making power under Article 213 cannot be used as a substitute for which body's law-making power?
faqs.e: The Court described repeated re-promulgation of ordinances as a "fraud on the constitution."

faqs.q: In M.C. Mehta vs. Union of India (1986), popularly known as the Oleum Gas Leak case, the Supreme Court introduced which new principle of liability in place of the earlier principle of strict liability?
faqs.e: The Court held that compensation applications under Article 32 are maintainable for enforcement of the right to life under Article 21.

faqs.q: Kihoto Hollohan vs. Zachillhu (1992) declared paragraph 7 of the Tenth Schedule unconstitutional for violating which Article?
faqs.e: Paragraph 7 excluded the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts without ratification by half the State Legislatures, as required for amendments affecting Article 368(2).

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indra Sawhney case (1992):
(I) The Court upheld 27% reservation for OBCs under Article 16(4)
(II) The Court upheld an additional 10% reservation for economically backward sections not covered by existing schemes
(III) The judgement led to the exclusion of the creamy layer among OBCs
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Court actually invalidated the 10% additional reservation order for economically backward sections, making statement (II) false.

faqs.q: The Indra Sawhney case led to the establishment of a statutory National Commission to examine complaints regarding the list of backward classes; this Commission is known as the:
Mohini Jain vs. State of Karnataka (1992), the Capitation Fee case, declared the right to education a fundamental right flowing from which Article?
The Unni Krishnan case (1993) held that children have a fundamental right to free education only up to what age?
faqs.e: Beyond this age, the state's obligation to provide education was held to depend on its economic capacity. This case's reasoning led to the 86th Amendment Act (2002), which inserted Article 21A.

faqs.q: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association vs. Union of India (1993), the Second Judges case, changed the meaning of the word "consultation" in Articles 124(2) and 217(1) to that of:
faqs.e: The Court held that the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court should be appointed Chief Justice of India, overruling the S.P. Gupta case (1981), the First Judges case.

faqs.q: The procedure for appointing judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts that emerged from the Second Judges case (1993) and the Third Judges case (1998) is popularly known as the:

Consider the following propositions laid down in S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India (1994) regarding Article 356:
(I) The validity of the President's proclamation under Article 356(1) is subject to judicial review
(II) The burden lies on the Union Government to prove that relevant material existed to justify the proclamation
(III) If a proclamation is held invalid, the court cannot restore the Legislative Assembly even if Parliament has approved it
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Court actually held that if the proclamation is held invalid, it is open for the court to restore the Legislative Assembly and Ministry, notwithstanding parliamentary approval — making statement (III) false.

faqs.q: S.R. Bommai vs. Union of India (1994) held that which principle is part of the basic structure, such that anti-secular acts of a State Government can justify President's Rule?
Vishaka vs. State of Rajasthan (1997) held that sexual harassment of women at the workplace violates which Articles of the Constitution?
faqs.e: The guidelines issued in this case, known as the Vishaka Guidelines, filled the legislative vacuum until the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 was enacted.

faqs.q: Vineet Narain vs. Union of India (1997), the Jain Hawala case, directed that statutory status should be conferred upon which body?
faqs.e: This led to the enactment of the CVC Act, 2003. The judgement also struck down the Single Directive requiring prior government permission to investigate senior officers, though this was later reinstated by the Act.

faqs.q: In Union of India vs. Association for Democratic Reforms (2002), the Poll Reforms case, the Supreme Court held that a voter's right to know a candidate's antecedents forms part of the freedom guaranteed under:
faqs.e: The Court directed the Election Commission to make candidates furnish details of criminal cases, assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications.

faqs.q: T.M.A. Pai Foundation vs. State of Karnataka (2002) held that for determining "minority" status under Article 30, the relevant unit is:
faqs.e: Since state reorganization has been on linguistic lines, religious and linguistic minorities must be considered state-wise.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act was enacted to overcome the effect of the T.M.A. Pai judgement and the Inamdar case (2005), inserting Clause (5) into Article 15?
Union of India vs. Naveen Jindal (2004) held that the right to fly the national flag with respect and dignity is a fundamental right under which Article?
faqs.e: The Court clarified this right cannot be exercised for commercial purposes.

faqs.q: Prakash Singh vs. Union of India (2006) issued seven directives on police reforms, including a minimum tenure of two years for which post, to be selected from the three senior-most officers empanelled by the UPSC?
M. Nagaraj vs. Union of India (2006) upheld the validity of Constitutional Amendment Acts inserting which two clauses into Article 16, enabling reservation in promotions for SCs and STs?
faqs.e: The Court held these amendments must still respect the ceiling of 50% and the concept of creamy layer, as laid down in the Indra Sawhney case (1992).

faqs.q: I.R. Coelho vs. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), the Ninth Schedule case, reaffirmed the ruling of which earlier case regarding the date after which Ninth Schedule additions are open to challenge?
Aruna Ramachandra Shanbaug vs. Union of India (2011) held that passive euthanasia is permissible, but any decision to withdraw life support requires approval from which authority?
faqs.e: Active euthanasia and assisted death remain illegal; the High Court Bench must seek the opinion of a committee of three doctors before deciding.

faqs.q: People's Union for Civil Liberties vs. Union of India (2013), the NOTA case, directed the Election Commission to introduce a "None of the Above" option primarily to protect a voter's:

options.a: Secrecy of not casting a vote

faqs.a: Secrecy of not casting a vote
faqs.e: The Court held that Rules 41(2), (3) and 49-O of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 were ultra vires Article 19(1)(a) to the extent they violated this secrecy.

faqs.q: Lily Thomas vs. Union of India (2013) struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, holding that disqualification of a convicted legislator takes effect:

options.a: Only if imprisonment exceeds two years
options.b: Only after the appeal period lapses
options.c: Immediately from the date of conviction

faqs.a: Immediately from the date of conviction
faqs.e: The Court held Parliament lacks power under Articles 102 and 191 to create different disqualification rules for sitting members versus prospective candidates.

faqs.q: T.S.R. Subramanian vs. Union of India (2013) directed that civil servants should not act on verbal instructions, and that such instructions must instead be:

options.b: Ratified by the Cadre Controlling Authority
options.d: Approved by the Civil Service Board

faqs.q: National Legal Services Authority vs. Union of India (2014) declared transgender persons, along with Hijras/Eunuchs, as a:
faqs.e: The Court held Article 21 protects the right of self-determination of gender identity, leading to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

faqs.q: Shreya Singhal vs. Union of India (2015) struck down Section 66A of which Act for being violative of Article 19(1)(a)?
faqs.e: The Court held the section was vague and over-broad, and not saved by the reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

faqs.q: The Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association case of 2015, popularly known as the Fourth Judges case or NJAC case, declared which Amendment Act unconstitutional for affecting the independence of the judiciary?
faqs.e: The Court also struck down the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act, 2014, restoring the earlier collegium system.

faqs.q: Shayara Bano vs. Union of India (2017), the Triple Talaq case, declared "talaq-e-biddat" unconstitutional for violating which Article?
faqs.e: The Court held this form of talaq manifestly arbitrary and also declared Section 2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 void to that extent. This led to the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

faqs.q: K.S. Puttaswamy vs. Union of India (2017) declared the right to privacy a fundamental right, protected as an intrinsic part of which Article?
faqs.e: The Court laid down a three-fold test for invasion of privacy: legality, need, and proportionality.

faqs.q: The K.S. Puttaswamy judgement overruled two earlier decisions that had held privacy is not constitutionally protected; these were the M.P. Sharma case (1954) and which other case?
Indian Young Lawyers Association vs. State of Kerala (2018), the Sabarimala case, struck down which rule that prohibited entry of women aged 10–50 into the temple?

options.a: Rule 3(b) of the Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship (Authorisation of Entry) Rules, 1965
options.c: Rule 49-O of the Conduct of Election Rules

faqs.a: Rule 3(b) of the Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship (Authorisation of Entry) Rules, 1965
faqs.e: The ban was held to violate Articles 14, 21 and 25.

faqs.q: Joseph Shine vs. Union of India (2018) decriminalised adultery by striking down which Section of the Indian Penal Code?
faqs.e: The Court also struck down Section 198(2) CrPC to the extent it applied to adultery; adultery remains a civil wrong and ground for divorce.

faqs.q: Navtej Singh Johar vs. Union of India (2018) decriminalised homosexuality by partly striking down which Section of the Indian Penal Code?
faqs.e: This overruled the earlier Suresh Kumar Koushal case (2013), which had upheld Section 377's validity.

faqs.q: M. Siddiq vs. Mahant Suresh Das (2019), the Ayodhya case, awarded the disputed land to which party?
faqs.e: The Court also directed allotment of 5 acres of alternative land to the UP Sunni Central Waqf Board and overturned the 2010 Allahabad High Court judgement, which had divided the land three ways.

faqs.q: Anuradha Bhasin vs. Union of India (2020) held that an order suspending internet services indefinitely is impermissible under which Rules?

options.a: Temporary Suspension of Telecom Services (Public Emergency or Public Safety) Rules, 2017

faqs.a: Temporary Suspension of Telecom Services (Public Emergency or Public Safety) Rules, 2017
faqs.e: The Court held that access to the internet enjoys protection under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g), subject to the test of proportionality.

faqs.q: Rambabu Singh Thakur vs. Sunil Arora (2020) directed political parties to publish criminal antecedents of selected candidates, with reasons for selection based on:
faqs.e: The Court explicitly held that mere winnability could not be the basis for selection reasons; this led to the Election Commission's Form C-7.

faqs.q: Internet and Mobile Association of India vs. Reserve Bank of India (2020) struck down an RBI circular banning dealings in virtual currencies for violating which Article?
faqs.e: The Court applied the test of proportionality, noting the RBI had not shown any actual loss suffered by banks due to virtual currency exchanges.

options.a: A.K. Gopalan vs. State of Madras
options.b: Satwant Singh Sawhney vs. D. Ramarathnam
options.c: Kharak Singh vs. State of U.P.
options.d: Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India

faqs.a: Satwant Singh Sawhney vs. D. Ramarathnam
faqs.e: Decided in 1967, this was one of the earliest cases expanding Article 21 beyond mere physical liberty. See table below for the full list of rights read into Article 21 through subsequent cases.

faqs.q: In which year did the Supreme Court, in Olga Tellis vs. Bombay Municipal Corporation, recognise the right to livelihood as part of Article 21?
faqs.e: This case is popularly known as the Pavement Dwellers case.

faqs.q: The doctrine of severability is also known by which other name?
Which Article of the Constitution forms the basis of the doctrine of severability?

Consider the following statements regarding Article 13:
(I) Article 13(1) deals with pre-constitution laws
(II) Article 13(2) deals with post-constitution laws and prohibits the State from making laws that abridge fundamental rights
(III) Under Article 13(2), such a law is void in its entirety even if only one provision violates fundamental rights
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Under the doctrine of severability, only the offending portion of a law is declared void, not the whole of it — making statement (III) incorrect.

faqs.q: According to the doctrine of severability, if the invalid part of a law cannot be separated from the valid part, what is the effect?

options.a: The law is suspended until amended
options.b: The law remains valid pending judicial review
options.c: Only the invalid part is struck down
options.d: The entire law is declared void

faqs.a: The entire law is declared void
